title: Real runtime topology
summary: The live Studio path separates the HTTP front from the semantic application path: an HTTP/HTTPS front serves browser assets and bootstrap configuration; the browser Wire runtime uses WebSocket to the Queue Fabric Web Gateway; the gateway bridges privately to the same authoritative ObjectQueueManager/Wire UI Server/Builder application. The HTTP front may be Node, ooRexx HTTP/HTTPS or another conforming implementation if it preserves the exact URL/MIME/bootstrap contract.
invariants: A browser shell loading is not proof that Queue backend/semantic state is alive.
A WebSocket 101 upgrade proves transport establishment, not synchronized Wire state.
The HTTP front must not contain Builder business truth or become a JSON business API.
Browser must not choose arbitrary Queue Fabric queues or receive claim tokens.
Changing the HTTP front for qualification must not simultaneously change Browser JS, gateway, definitions or application state.

provenance.claim: Accepted executable baseline and consumer-neutral Builder authority.
Development/recovery evidence; does not supersede the accepted v0.11 executable baseline.
